entries.reason: Guards that adaptive allocation in an analysis run cuts the rare row's cross-session noise at least 5x without biasing any row's mean; the claim is statistical, so it needs two arms of thirty full sessions and cannot shrink without losing the power to see a 5x variance ratio.

Shared setup of the relative-anchor additivity sentinel: six runs (the whole scene and its two halves, under each exposure anchor), which the file's tests all read; the opposition between the two anchors is only visible across all six.

Guards the fixed-seed contract of analysis runs across ten sessions of one server (a worker RNG that was not re-seeded broke it); ten sessions is the shape of the defect, since it only appears after the first.

Guards that the device-fused GPU route publishes the same exposure anchor as legacy CPU, judged against the anchor's own measured seed-to-seed spread; that spread has to be measured in the test, which costs several full runs per route.

Shared setup of the fp32 accumulation hot-pixel test: one long legacy CPU run, because the defect (a float32 running sum drifting a hot pixel's colour) only appears once a pixel has taken about 1e7 adds; already cut to the smallest budget that still shows it.

Proves the projection battery's routing assertion can fail, by requesting a route the build cannot honour; without it every per-projection Metal parity result could be a silent legacy fallback, and observing the route needs real sessions.

Guards against the GPU colour-mask batch leak (a layer-0 carried mask never reset between batches, which skewed per-class ratios 3-7x between CPU and Metal); the leak only shows once a run spans many dispatch batches, so the 4M-ray budget is what makes it reachable.

Guards against a Metal session serving two renderers collapsing to a fraction of single-renderer throughput (CI runs the disaster profile: 0.75 over 5 interleaved reps; the precise 0.85 over 21 runs on the reference machines on a schedule). Its cost is the interleaved repetitions a median ratio needs on a runner whose per-arm CoV is 0.155-0.229; fewer reps raise the false-red rate at this threshold.

Metal exit-seam parity against legacy CPU on a multi-scattering scene at ms_prob 0.8, the deepest cross-layer transit in the battery; the legacy CPU oracle arm dominates the cost and the ray budget is what lets block-mean correlation separate a real mismatch from Monte-Carlo speckle.

Guards that adaptive allocation in an analysis run cuts the rare row's cross-session noise at least 5x without biasing any row's mean; the claim is statistical, so it needs two arms of thirty full sessions and cannot shrink without losing the power to see a 5x variance ratio.

Per-renderer Metal-vs-legacy-CPU parity when one session serves several renderers (N device planes); the only coverage of the N-plane path, and each renderer's plane has to be compared against its own legacy oracle run.
Guards that changing the Metal dispatch batch does not change the statistical result and that commits conserve rays; it has to run the same scene at several batch sizes, each a full run.

Metal exit-seam parity against legacy CPU on a low-symmetry cone crystal with a B filter, the case where label and physical symmetry diverge; a filtered sparse scene needs this ray budget before its correlation threshold means anything.

Guards the fixed-seed contract of analysis runs across ten sessions of one server (a worker RNG that was not re-seeded broke it); ten sessions is the shape of the defect, since it only appears after the first.

Metal exit-seam parity against legacy CPU for multi-scattering with a compound filter expression; the only end-to-end check that both routes apply the same filter grammar across layers, on a sparse image that needs this budget.

Metal exit-seam parity against legacy CPU for multi-scattering at ms_prob 0.8 with a raypath filter, which is where filter-fail rays must stop propagating across layers on both routes; sparse filtered output needs this budget to be judged.

Proves the routing assertion every other Metal parity test relies on can fail (a request the build cannot honour reads back as a different route); without it a silent fallback to legacy CPU would make the whole battery vacuous, and it has to create real sessions to observe the route.

Guards that the device-fused GPU route publishes the same exposure anchor as legacy CPU, judged against the anchor's own measured seed-to-seed spread; that spread has to be measured in the test, which costs several full runs per route.

Guards that a device-fused GPU route hands over the globe's far-side energy plane (dropping it silently draws the wrong clip, with no error); compared on the finished CLI image against legacy CPU, which is the only place the defect is visible.

Shared setup of the relative-anchor additivity sentinel: six runs (the whole scene and its two halves, under each exposure anchor), which the file's tests all read; the opposition between the two anchors is only visible across all six.

Shared setup of the fp32 accumulation hot-pixel test: one long legacy CPU run, because the defect (a float32 running sum drifting a hot pixel's colour) only appears once a pixel has taken about 1e7 adds; already cut to the smallest budget that still shows it.

Smoke render of the colour-class example config against its committed reference at a calibrated PSNR threshold; the threshold was calibrated at this ray budget, so cutting the budget means reshooting the reference and recalibrating.

Smoke render of the multi-scattering example config against its committed reference at a calibrated PSNR threshold; the threshold was calibrated at this ray budget, so cutting the budget means reshooting the reference and recalibrating.

End-to-end sanity for entry-point incidence sampling on the 22-degree halo scene: two independent CLI renders must agree to the Monte-Carlo noise floor; the analytic oracles are the primary judge, and this leg needs a budget where that floor is measurable.

End-to-end sanity for entry-point incidence sampling on the plate parhelion scene: two independent CLI renders must agree to the Monte-Carlo noise floor; the analytic oracles are the primary judge, and this leg needs a budget where that floor is measurable.

Pins the schema3 report contract that an exhausted evaluation budget lands as outcome=partial with termination=6 source curves, not as a physical stop or silent absorption: the cap interrupts the final source curve inside its optical bracket while the other report stages still complete. The claim needs two full CLI report runs on the 3-1-5 scene (capped at 405930 optical evaluations plus the unconstrained comparison), so the cost is the engine's own report work; the contract spans CLI args through the engine to the JSON verdict, so no cheaper layer carries it.

phase_budgets.reason: Two conditions; the authoritative ruler is the adaptive per-miss limit overhead_seconds + max_seconds_per_miss * misses, measured by collect_cache_stats.py after the zeroed-per-run build. Calibration: warm 0-miss builds measure 15-21s (x1.4 -> overhead 30); the worst legal class measured 4.06 s/miss on 121 misses (run 39158418638), x1.15 runner tier +7% -> 5.0. All five zero-test-failure reds of the 420s era replay green under both conditions: 436.6s/156, 421.2s/163, 552.9s/162, 602.7s/208, 490.8s/121 misses (runs 38124925035, 38254590460, 38320486746, 39061707245, 39158418638). max_seconds re-anchored 720 -> 1800 on 2026-10-19; dominant term: the #514 deployment gap — 720 was derived from the worst-observed legal build (602.7s x1.15 = 693), a sample maximum the healthy envelope then outgrew: run 39197233020 built a broad closure at 722.5s / 375 misses / 1.93 s/miss, healthy under the adaptive limit (30 + 5.0x375 = 1905s) and red at 720 by 2.5s with 0 tests failed. New derivation: envelope = 1.15 x (30 + 1.93x375 + 4.06x(524-375)) = 1561s, x1.15 closure-diversity headroom -> 1795 -> 1800; the full-tree signature is 524 compile requests measured on this leg's build definition, and the 149-TU unmeasured tail is priced at this leg's own worst class 4.06 s/miss. The s/miss ratios quoted here include the run's own ~30s overhead, double-counting ~2% against the formula's separate overhead term — conservative, on the backstop's safe side. A second adjustment of any constant here within 60 days of 2026-10-19 requires a structural task. Known single-K blind spot: per-miss regressions on lighter classes (2.58-3.41 s/miss observed) stay green up to ~72%; calibration and sensitivity are recorded in doc/testing/testing-architecture.md §7.7.

The 360-second ceiling is retained unchanged; the 2026-10-20 red was disposed by suite composition (a zero-sum test-value rebalance), not by raising the constant. Reds, phase-internal ctest.json seconds: 381.4 (PR #532 attempt1, run 39477672688) and 380.2/380.6 on main (725018d3/a4d56f09) - the main reds show this leg had also crossed into steady-state red on the trunk. Composition mirrors the Windows leg's finding: serial, compute-dominated, two runner tiers (u-fast 225.6-227.3 vs slow 380.2-381.4 on the same 3629-case suite), so the constraint case is the slow tier. Machine-speed normalization (registry v4, 2026-10-23) supersedes the tier bookkeeping as the gate mechanism: the effective budget is max_seconds x factor, factor = median measured/calibrated ratio over the 7-id ruler subset, calibrated to the fast tier (median over runs 39618759900, 39803894177, 39890258136, 39865840416 - the samples whose suite-wide median row ratio reads <= 1.05). The 2026-10-22/23 incident reds - 386.8 (run 39863154753), 386.1 (run 39868769974), 466.9 (run 39765273305) - replay green at factors 1.64/1.64/1.65 (effective budgets ~591-595s) with 0 test failures: the host fleet had drifted to a slower tier (row-level median ratios cluster at 1.0 / ~1.2 / ~1.6 on this leg), and the 726 two-tier picture (slow = fast x ~1.67) is dissolved by the normalization rather than by re-anchoring the constant. Attribution note for run 39765273305: its Windows leg's ruler reading of 0.999 proved +103.8s of that run's cost to be branch-new tests, not host drift, so this leg's replay-green absorbs the factor-carried host component on top of that real branch cost - a pure host-tier attribution would hide that a branch day can add ~100s of suite cost and still pass. Ruler selection: ids whose calibrated reading is >= 2s, ranked by cross-run ratio concentration (median |log ratio deviation from the suite's tier median|), screened for deterministic pure-compute workloads (no wall-clock deadline drives the workload; the Schema3 chain's budget_ms=120000 is a safety cap - the evaluations count ends the run) and low source churn; all seven ids are present and non-zero in every one of the 48 sampled runs. Negative control: +30% on the non-ruler rows of a fast green sample stays red (normalization does not absorb non-ruler regressions). Known blind spot (accepted, disclosed): a uniform slowdown on exactly the code the rulers execute is absorbed by the factor; the per-test 2x entries, the absolute perf legs, and the per-run factor in the green notice (drift trend) are the compensating controls; band exceeded reads ::warning with the raw factor. A second adjustment of the ruler set, calibration or band within 60 days of 2026-10-23 requires a structural task with paired samples. Adjudication and ledger are shared with the Windows leg's record (see the Windows MSVC x86_64 ctest entry): cut the duplicated random/early-stop routing-key negative, fold the mc_attribution living A/B pair into the production cases, share one deterministic Lowitz assembly across three tests, move the C-API prefix-defaults case onto a single-member plate. This leg releases 39.4s against 0 added; slow-tier replay of the reds lands 340.8-342.1s against 360. Margin = 5s, the same derivation as the Windows leg - the bound computes ~3.0s there and 5s is adopted as the integer cushion; this leg's inputs are smaller (attempt span 0.37s, row-level p95 1.7% vs 4.0%), so the same cushion covers it. Rejected alternatives: per-miss/adaptive ctest budgeting (no cache-miss analogue exists for a serial test phase) and runner parallelization (owner-level resource-semantics change; does not govern suite composition). The machine_factor block supersedes the rejected-alternatives line's absolute-wall-clock premise: the owner's zero-sum ruling governs suite composition and stays in force; normalization prices the host, not the suite.

The mechanism's red side is pinned by the same wave's one genuine red: run 39765273305 measured 506.8s with the ruler reading 0.999 - its +103.8s over the fast tier is the branch's own new WarmContract tests (four cases at ~24s each that are 0.03s placeholders on the base branch), and the normalization correctly leaves it red. Ruler selection, blind-spot disclosure, negative control and the 60-day anti-ratchet clause are recorded once in the Ubuntu x86_64 ctest entry and apply here verbatim. Adjudication (zero-sum: new entrants must prove the defect they guard or lose their slot; incumbents keep unless positive redundancy evidence): cut RandomAndEarlyStopDocumentsCarryNoFamilyRoutingKey (its full-dimensional half duplicated RandomPrismLiteral's key assertion verbatim; the early-stop half moved one line into LiteralScopeKeepsOnlyTheRequestedSequence), fold the mc_attribution living A/B pair into the production Schema3 cases (identical shapes rerunning the same statistical fact; the unit-only assertions moved with them), share one deterministic Lowitz assembly across its three read-side tests, and move the C-API prefix-defaults case onto a single-member plate (its subject is the ABI contract, not the crystal; the red-state probe still trips it). Ledger: 57.2s released (adjudicated; per-sample replay recomputes 57.1), 0 added; slow-tier replay of all five reds lands 440.2-443.1s against 480. Margin = 5s, adopted as the integer conservative cushion over the derivation bound 1.15 x (0.72s attempt-to-attempt span + 1.4s row-level p95 propagation + 0.5s binary-gap drift) = 3.0s (the 3.0 -> 5.0 step covers out-of-sample row-matrix effects), over 16 paired artifacts; per-test registration stays empty by design (the largest member is ~35s, under the 60s registration floor). Rejected alternatives: per-miss/adaptive ctest budgeting (a serial test phase has no cache-miss analogue to price) and runner parallelization (a phase resource-semantics change at owner level, and it leaves the suite composition - the actual cost driver - ungoverned).
